~ Susan M. (06:30):
In regards to the equity argument - "Educational equity means that every child receives what they need to develop to their full academic and social potential." This is often discussed in education - the heart of all differentiation - equity does NOT mean equal!

~ Susan M. (06:33):
Funding wise - this is not my expertise but a few things: 1) No, Maya Lin is not a title 1 school so can't get title 1 funding; 2) Free and Reduced Lunch (FRL) numbers, from the state I see 36.5% https://www.cde.ca.gov/ds/ad/filessp.asp but from Karen's SSC Slides I see 38% https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1anX6X6QyM7MlG1-9F7-c677tfs6yWsc-heuQZVYY_gs/edit?slide=id.gf5d56dd250_0_17#slide=id.gf5d56dd250_0_17

~ Susan M. (06:36):
actually acronym is FRMP (not FRL)

~ Susan M. (06:37):
3) Prop 28 - Intent of Prop 28 is to provide ADDITIONAL arts funding not less arts funding (supplement NOT supplant).. https://www.cde.ca.gov/eo/in/prop28artsandmusicedfundingfaq.asp
Do any "supplement not supplant" requirements apply to Arts and Music in Schools (AMS)? (Updated 22-Apr-2024) (https://www.cde.ca.gov/eo/in/prop28artsandmusicedfundingfaq.asp#do-any-supplement-not-supplant-requirements-apply-to-arts-and-music-in-schools-ams-updated-22-apr-2024)
Yes, California Education Code (EC)Chapter 5.1, Section 8820, subdivision (g), paragraph (2), states that as a condition of receipt of funds pursuant to this chapter, a local educational agency (LEA) shall annually: “Certify that such funds received will be used to supplement funding for arts education programs and that funds received in the prior fiscal year were, in fact, used to supplement arts education programs.” For the purpose of this program, “supplement” means that the funds appropriated by this chapter shall be used by LEAs to increase funding of arts education programs and not to supplant existing funding for those programs (ECSection 8821[e]). The California Department of Education (CDE) recommends that each LEA seek guidance from their legal counsel for guidance relative to their annual usage of AMS funds and whether they can make this certification each year. The CDE is not approving or denying individual LEA requests for allowable expenditures. All expenditures should be consistent with statute. Additional guidance for LEAs to demonstrate compliance with this requirement for the purpose of the annual audit (i.e., example worksheets, etc.) is available on the CDE Proposition 28 —AMS Financial & Audit Requirements (https://www.cde.ca.gov/eo/in/prop28auditresource.asp) web page.

Sarah (21:18):
I attended our monthly LCAP committee meeting tonight and had a good chat with assistant superintendent Kirsten Zazo and got some helpful updates from the district about the current budget. Passing along the most important points here for our group:
- There are no schools in the district anticipating leftover prop 28 funds, so we can probably save Ms. Ringewald the effort of asking around.
- The budget reserves are there to make sure we can pay our bills for the next 3 years and are intended as a bulwark against shifting state budgets. The way CA's tax code is written, school funding is highly dependent on the taxes paid by a few wealthy individuals and can fluctuate wildly. (I don't know much about this, so just relaying what I was told by Shariq Khan, Assistant Superintendent of Business Services for AUSD)
- The funding that is ending for Ms. Moore's position was from a one-time block grant, so it's not that the general funds for art are being cut, but that that one time money is ending.
- The district has maintained the same level of general funding for the arts since 2022 (the year Prop 28 passed)
- I explained to Zazo that we were only notified last Spring of the ending in funding for the art teacher, and she agreed that's a problem. I also mentioned that this means our PTA needs to raise $280K in one year and she was shocked.
- Zazo is happy to meet with me/us to talk about how arts funding is allocated across the district and to prepare for meeting with Scuderi (she will also likely attend that meeting).
- For our meetings with the Board, she suggests focusing on how important arts is to the school and the students. She urges us not to focus on whether we deserve funding based on our demographics (since there are schools like Ruby that have way bigger needs -- more than 80% unduplicated students).
- She would like to understand why Maya Lin is paying for a school nurse, as health-related positions should be fully covered by the district. <This message was edited>

LCAP has ~$9 million to disburse annually and the committee looks at the best way to distribute the funds across schools focusing on the most disadvantaged student groups. The hope is to talk with PTAC about making the funds go further by leveraging more coordinated efforts across schools. If anyone else is interested in LCAP you are welcome to join, it's open to everyone in Alameda! <This message was edited>

Jamie Martinez (21:49):
Hi @all this was shared with me by a Maya Lin parent who’s also an AUSD teacher… something we should look into as part of the conversation regarding Prop 28 funds:

In January AB2440 will come into effect, which clarifies a lot of questions from the original Prop 28 legislation. There were a few things that I thought were interesting and applied to our situation.

AB2440 makes it so the district can pool funds between schools. This means, for example, they could combine funds from 2 different schools to fund a position, as long as it is within the district. As we know, Prop 28 funds must be spent within a 3 year window otherwise they go back to the state, so this June 2027 the allocation from the 24/25 school year has to be spent or returned by June 2027. Something to look into might be if we have any schools in the district that have funding from the 24/25 school year that they are not going to spend and would otherwise be returned. Perhaps that funding could be pooled to be used this year to pay a portion of Ms. Moore's salary, thereby reserving the funds from this year's allocation so they could go towards next year? I know that sounds a little convoluted, but maybe worth a look into. It wouldn't be a permanent fix going forward, but it might help get us over the hump and buy some time. I wonder what our larger secondary schools that were already fully staffed with art, music, etc have been doing with their money? It is supposed to be publically available on each school's website, but I've never seen it. The district level report is a joke.

AB2440 also clarified the supplement not supplant rule. Basically it is looked at from the district level, not per school site, so if the district spent 100k last year on the arts, they would have to spend at least that this year - minus any funding that disappeared (grants, pta) and plus this year's prop 28 allocation. Also, if they had declining enrollment they are within their rights to eliminate positions and rehire with prop 28 funds.

https://calmatters.digitaldemocracy.org/bills/ca_202520260ab2440
